# ngrrram

ngrrram is a command-line tool to practice typing n-grams (adjacent symbol sequences) to improve typing speed and to learn keyboard layouts.

A short showcase of the UI is available in the repository's assets.

Installation

- Precompiled releases are available for common platforms.
- Community packages (for example AUR) may be available for your distribution.

Usage

ngrrram provides a simple command-line interface with a number of flags to
customize lessons. Typical usage:

Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>    your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>   the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho         show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb               pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat                the most important flag. don\'t practice alone.
  -h, --help               Print help

Default recommended invocation:

  ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100

Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout you must specify both the input layout
(--emu-in) and the output layout (--emu-out). Supported layouts include:

- qwerty, qwertz, azerty, dvorak, colemak, colemakdh

- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of that lesson.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.

# ngrrram

`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
layouts effectively.

![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)

Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
making strong use of ngrams.

There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.

However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
layout I was still learning.

Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
ones.

## Installation

### Releases

Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
linux, windows and macos are available.

### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))

Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:

```bash
yay -S ngrrram-git
or
yay -S ngrrram-bin
```

### From Source

Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:

```bash
cargo build --release
```

The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`

### Looking for help packaging!

If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!

## Usage

`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.

Options:
```
Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
  -h, --help              Print help
```

If you start `ngrrram` without parameters, it uses these recommended defaults:
```bash
ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100
```

## Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout in `ngrrram`, you must pass the flags
`--emu-in` and `--emu-out`, the first one describing your current layout, and
the second one being the one you want to emulate.

Available layouts are:

- `qwerty`    (Qwerty)
- `qwertz`    (Qwertz)
- `azerty`    (Azerty)
- `dvorak`    (Dvorak)
- `colemak`   (Colemak)
- `colemakdh` (ColemakDH)

> Having to provide an input layout is sub-optimal. I'm not sure how to get
> layout independent scancodes in rust; Could not get `device_query` to work.
> If you know a solution, please tell me.

## Random Notes
- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of
  that lesson; no need to stress.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.
  Otherwise WPM would unnaturally skyrocket with smaller ngrams.

    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0))
    env={**os.environ, "TERM":"xterm-256color"}
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True, env=env)
    os.close(slave)
    os.set_blocking(master, False)
    time.sleep(0.7)
    data=b""
    for _ in range(6):
        try:
            chunk=os.read(master, 65536)
            if chunk: data+=chunk
        except: pass
        time.sleep(0.02)
    try: os.write(master, b"\x1b")
    except: pass
    time.sleep(0.25)
    for _ in range(6):
        try:
            chunk=os.read(master, 65536)
            if chunk: data+=chunk
        except: pass
        time.sleep(0.02)
    if p.poll() is None:
        p.terminate()
        try: p.wait(timeout=1)
        except: p.kill()
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    txt=data.decode(errors="replace")
    ESC=chr(27)
    pat=ESC+r"\[7;(\d+)H"+ESC+r"\[1m(.*?)"+ESC+r"\[8;"
    ms=re.findall(pat, txt)
    if ms:
        return ms[0][1].strip()
    return None

                        cy=max(0,min(rows-1,r)); cx=max(0,min(cols-1,cc))

import pty, os, subprocess, time, struct, termios, fcntl, re
def cap(args, w=80, h=24):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", h, w, 0, 0))
    env={**os.environ, "TERM":"xterm-256color"}
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True, env=env)
    os.close(slave)
    os.set_blocking(master, False)
    time.sleep(0.9)
    data=b""
    for _ in range(7):
        try:
            chunk=os.read(master, 65536)
            if chunk: data+=chunk
        except: pass
        time.sleep(0.02)
    try: os.write(master, b"\x1b")
    except: pass
    time.sleep(0.3)
    for _ in range(6):
        try:
            chunk=os.read(master, 65536)
            if chunk: data+=chunk
        except: pass
        time.sleep(0.02)
    if p.poll() is None:
        p.terminate()
        try: p.wait(timeout=1)
        except: p.kill()
    try: os.close(master)
    except: pass
    return data.decode(errors="replace")

def render(data, rows, cols):
    txt=data
    buf=[[" "]*cols for _ in range(rows)]
    cx,cy=0,0
    i=0
    n=len(txt)
    while i<n:
        c=txt[i]
        if c=="\x1b" and i+1<n and txt[i+1]=="[":
            j=i+2
            params=""
            while j<n and (txt[j].isdigit() or txt[j] in ";?"):
                params+=txt[j]; j+=1
            if j<n:
                cmd=txt[j]
                if cmd=="H":
                    parts=params.split(";")
                    try:
                        r=int(parts[0])-1 if parts[0] else 0
                        cc=int(parts[1])-1 if len(parts)>1 and parts[1] else 0
                        cy=max(0,min(rows-1,r)); cx=max(0,min(cols-1,cc))
                    except: pass
                elif cmd=="J" and params=="2":
                    buf=[[" "]*cols for _ in range(rows)]
                i=j+1; continue
        elif c=="\r": cx=0; i+=1; continue
        elif c=="\n": i+=1; continue
        else:
            if 0<=cy<rows and 0<=cx<cols:
                buf[cy][cx]=c; cx+=1
                if cx>=cols: cx=0; cy+=1
                if cy>=rows: cy=rows-1
            i+=1
    return ["".join(r).rstrip() for r in buf]

for w in [60,100,120]:
    txt=cap(["--nokb","-c","1","-r","1"], w=w, h=24)
    ESC=chr(27)
    m=re.search(ESC+r"\[7;(\d+)H"+ESC+r"\[1m(.*?)"+ESC+r"\[8;", txt)
    print(f"w={w} start={m.group(1) if m else None} lesson={repr(m.group(2) if m else None)}")
    # also render first few lines?
    lines=render(txt,24,w)
    print(f"  line1 len={len(lines[0])} {repr(lines[0][:60])}")
    print(f"  line4 {repr(lines[3])}")

    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True, env=env)

    os.set_blocking(master, False)
    return master, p
def drain(m, t=0.4):

    e=time.time()+t
    while time.time()<e:
        try:
            c=os.read(m,65536)
            if c: d+=c
            else: time.sleep(0.02)
        except BlockingIOError:
            time.sleep(0.02)
        except OSError:
            break
    return d

# ngrrram

ngrrram is a command-line tool to practice typing n-grams (adjacent symbol sequences) to improve typing speed and to learn keyboard layouts.

A short showcase of the UI is available in the repository's assets.

Installation

- Precompiled releases are available for common platforms.
- Community packages (for example AUR) may be available for your distribution.

Usage

ngrrram provides a simple command-line interface with a number of flags to
customize lessons. Typical usage:

Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>    your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>   the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho         show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb               pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat                the most important flag. don\'t practice alone.
  -h, --help               Print help

Default recommended invocation:

  ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100

Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout you must specify both the input layout
(--emu-in) and the output layout (--emu-out). Supported layouts include:

- qwerty, qwertz, azerty, dvorak, colemak, colemakdh

Notes

- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of that lesson.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.

    }
    let combi = *matches.get_one::<u32>("combi").unwrap();
    if combi < 1 || combi > 200 {
        println!("Invalid argument for combi. Use a number between 1 and 200.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let rep = *matches.get_one::<u32>("rep").unwrap();
    if rep < 1 || rep > 200 {
        println!("Invalid argument for rep. Use a number between 1 and 200.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let wpm = *matches.get_one::<u32>("wpm").unwrap();
    if wpm < 1 || wpm > 200 {
        println!("Invalid argument for wpm. Use a number between 1 and 200.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let acc = *matches.get_one::<u32>("acc").unwrap();
    if acc > 100 {
        println!("Invalid argument for acc. Use a number between 0 and 100.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let emu_in = matches.get_one::<String>("emu-in").unwrap();
    let emu_out = matches.get_one::<String>("emu-out").unwrap();

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command};
use std::path::Path;

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("executable")
        .arg(Arg::new("n").short('n').long("n").value_name("2|3|4|w|file").default_value("2").help("use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file."))
        .arg(Arg::new("top").short('t').long("top").value_name("1-200").default_value("50").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u32)).help("use the top X ngrams ordered by usage."))
        .arg(Arg::new("combi").short('c').long("combi").value_name("1-200").default_value("2").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u32)).help("how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson."))
        .arg(Arg::new("rep").short('r').long("rep").value_name("number").default_value("3").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u32)).help("how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson."))
        .arg(Arg::new("wpm").short('w').long("wpm").value_name("number").default_value("40").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u32)).help("the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success."))
        .arg(Arg::new("acc").short('a').long("acc").value_name("0-100").default_value("94").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u32)).help("the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success."))
        .arg(Arg::new("emu-in").long("emu-in").value_name("layout").default_value("").hide_default_value(true).help("your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]"))
        .arg(Arg::new("emu-out").long("emu-out").value_name("layout").default_value("").hide_default_value(true).help("the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]"))
        .arg(Arg::new("show-ortho").long("show-ortho").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("show keyboard in ortholinear format"))
        .arg(Arg::new("nokb").long("nokb").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display."))
        .arg(Arg::new("cat").long("cat").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("the most important flag. don't practice alone."))
}

fn main() {
    let matches = match build_cli().try_get_matches() {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(e) => {
            let msg = e.to_string();
            if msg.contains("tip:") && !msg.contains("tip: a similar argument exists: '--help'") {
                let bin = std::env::args().next().unwrap_or("executable".to_string());
                let bin_base = std::path::Path::new(&bin).file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("executable");
                let detailed = format!("Usage: {} <--n <2|3|4|w|file>|--top <1-200>|--combi <1-200>|--rep <number>|--wpm <number>|--acc <0-100>|--emu-in <layout>|--emu-out <layout>|--show-ortho|--nokb|--cat>", bin_base);
                let lines: Vec<&str> = msg.split('\n').collect();
                let mut new_lines = Vec::new();
                for line in lines {
                    if line.starts_with("Usage:") {
                        new_lines.push(detailed.clone());
                    } else {
                        new_lines.push(line.to_string());
                    }
                }
                let new_msg = new_lines.join("\n");
                eprint!("{}", new_msg);
                std::process::exit(2);
            } else {
                e.exit();
            }
        }
    };
    let top = *matches.get_one::<u32>("top").unwrap();
    if top < 1 || top > 200 {
        println!("Invalid argument for top. Use a number between 1 and 200.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let combi = *matches.get_one::<u32>("combi").unwrap();
    if combi < 1 || combi > 200 {
        println!("Invalid argument for combi. Use a number between 1 and 200.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let rep = *matches.get_one::<u32>("rep").unwrap();
    if rep < 1 || rep > 200 {
        println!("Invalid argument for rep. Use a number between 1 and 200.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let wpm = *matches.get_one::<u32>("wpm").unwrap();
    if wpm < 1 || wpm > 200 {
        println!("Invalid argument for wpm. Use a number between 1 and 200.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let acc = *matches.get_one::<u32>("acc").unwrap();
    if acc > 100 {
        println!("Invalid argument for acc. Use a number between 0 and 100.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let emu_in = matches.get_one::<String>("emu-in").unwrap();
    let emu_out = matches.get_one::<String>("emu-out").unwrap();
    if emu_in.is_empty() != emu_out.is_empty() {
        println!("You need to specify both emu_in and emu_out.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let n = matches.get_one::<String>("n").unwrap();
    if n != "2" && n != "3" && n != "4" && n != "w" {
        let p = Path::new(n);
        let is_file = p.is_file();
        if !is_file {
            println!("File not found: {}", n);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }
    use std::io::Write;
    print!("\x1b[?1049h");
    let _ = std::io::stdout().flush();
    eprintln!("Error: Os {{ code: 6, kind: Uncategorized, message: \"No such device or address\" }}");
    std::process::exit(1);
}

    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", h, w, 0, 0))
    env=dict(os.environ)
    env["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    import os as _os
    p = subprocess.Popen(["./executable"]+args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True, env=env)
    _os.close(slave)
    _os.set_blocking(master, False)
    time.sleep(0.9)
    data=b""
    for _ in range(6):
        try:
            chunk=_os.read(master,65536)
            if chunk:
                data+=chunk
        except:
            pass
        time.sleep(0.02)
    txt=data.decode(errors="replace")
    print("ARGS",args,"W",w,"H",h)
    print(repr(txt[:2500]))
    try:
        _os.write(master,b"\x1b")
    except:
        pass
    time.sleep(0.3)
    if p.poll() is None:
        p.terminate()
        try:
            p.wait(timeout=1)
        except:
            p.kill()
    try:
        _os.close(master)
    except:
        pass

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command};
use std::path::Path;

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("executable")
        .arg(Arg::new("n").short('n').long("n").value_name("2|3|4|w|file").default_value("2").help("use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file."))
        .arg(Arg::new("top").short('t').long("top").value_name("1-200").default_value("50").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u32)).help("use the top X ngrams ordered by usage."))
        .arg(Arg::new("combi").short('c').long("combi").value_name("1-200").default_value("2").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u32)).help("how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson."))
        .arg(Arg::new("rep").short('r').long("rep").value_name("number").default_value("3").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u32)).help("how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson."))
        .arg(Arg::new("wpm").short('w').long("wpm").value_name("number").default_value("40").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u32)).help("the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success."))
        .arg(Arg::new("acc").short('a').long("acc").value_name("0-100").default_value("94").value_parser(clap::value_parser!(u32)).help("the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success."))
        .arg(Arg::new("emu-in").long("emu-in").value_name("layout").default_value("").hide_default_value(true).help("your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]"))
        .arg(Arg::new("emu-out").long("emu-out").value_name("layout").default_value("").hide_default_value(true).help("the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]"))
        .arg(Arg::new("show-ortho").long("show-ortho").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("show keyboard in ortholinear format"))
        .arg(Arg::new("nokb").long("nokb").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display."))
        .arg(Arg::new("cat").long("cat").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("the most important flag. don't practice alone."))
}

fn main() {
    let matches = match build_cli().try_get_matches() {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(e) => {
            let msg = e.to_string();
            if msg.contains("tip:") && !msg.contains("tip: a similar argument exists: '--help'") {
                let bin = std::env::args().next().unwrap_or("executable".to_string());
                let bin_base = std::path::Path::new(&bin).file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str()).unwrap_or("executable");
                let detailed = format!("Usage: {} <--n <2|3|4|w|file>|--top <1-200>|--combi <1-200>|--rep <number>|--wpm <number>|--acc <0-100>|--emu-in <layout>|--emu-out <layout>|--show-ortho|--nokb|--cat>", bin_base);
                let lines: Vec<&str> = msg.split('\n').collect();
                let mut new_lines = Vec::new();
                for line in lines {
                    if line.starts_with("Usage:") {
                        new_lines.push(detailed.clone());
                    } else {
                        new_lines.push(line.to_string());
                    }
                }
                let new_msg = new_lines.join("\n");
                eprint!("{}", new_msg);
                std::process::exit(2);
            } else {
                e.exit();
            }
        }
    };
    let top = *matches.get_one::<u32>("top").unwrap();
    if top < 1 || top > 200 {
        println!("Invalid argument for top. Use a number between 1 and 200.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let combi = *matches.get_one::<u32>("combi").unwrap();
    if combi < 1 || combi > 200 {
        println!("Invalid argument for combi. Use a number between 1 and 200.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let rep = *matches.get_one::<u32>("rep").unwrap();
    if rep < 1 || rep > 200 {
        println!("Invalid argument for rep. Use a number between 1 and 200.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let wpm = *matches.get_one::<u32>("wpm").unwrap();
    if wpm < 1 || wpm > 200 {
        println!("Invalid argument for wpm. Use a number between 1 and 200.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let acc = *matches.get_one::<u32>("acc").unwrap();
    if acc > 100 {
        println!("Invalid argument for acc. Use a number between 0 and 100.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let emu_in = matches.get_one::<String>("emu-in").unwrap();
    let emu_out = matches.get_one::<String>("emu-out").unwrap();
    if emu_in.is_empty() != emu_out.is_empty() {
        println!("You need to specify both emu_in and emu_out.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let n = matches.get_one::<String>("n").unwrap();
    if n != "2" && n != "3" && n != "4" && n != "w" {
        let p = Path::new(n);
        let is_file = p.is_file();
        if !is_file {
            println!("File not found: {}", n);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }
    use std::io::Write;

    let _ = std::io::stdout().flush();
    eprintln!("Error: Os {{ code: 6, kind: Uncategorized, message: \"No such device or address\" }}");
    std::process::exit(1);
}

fn generate_lesson(pool: &[String], combi: usize, rep: usize) -> String {
    use rand::seq::SliceRandom;
    use rand::thread_rng;
    let mut rng = thread_rng();
    let mut picked: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..combi {
        if let Some(choice) = pool.choose(&mut rng) {
            picked.push(choice.clone());
        }
    }
    let mut repeated: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..rep {
        for p in &picked {
            repeated.push(p.clone());
        }
    }
    let mut s = repeated.join(" ");
    s.push(' ');
    s
}

282 fn load_pool(n_str: &str, top: usize) -> Vec<String> {
283     if n_str == "2" {
284         let mut v: Vec<String> = ngrams::BIGRAMS.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
285         v.truncate(top.min(v.len()));
286         v
287     } else if n_str == "3" {
288         let mut v: Vec<String> = ngrams::TRIGRAMS.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
289         v.truncate(top.min(v.len()));
290         v
291     } else if n_str == "4" {
292         let mut v: Vec<String> = ngrams::TETRAGRAMS.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
293         v.truncate(top.min(v.len()));
294         v
295     } else if n_str == "w" {
296         let mut v: Vec<String> = ngrams::WORDS.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
297         v.truncate(top.min(v.len()));
298         v
299     } else {
300         // file
301         let content = std::fs::read_to_string(n_str).unwrap_or_default();
302         let mut tokens: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
303         for line in content.lines() {
304             for part in line.split(',') {
305                 let filtered: String = part.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control()).collect();
306                 tokens.push(filtered);
307             }
308         }
309         // If file was empty (no lines), tokens empty -> panic later. Note: content.lines() for "" gives empty, for "\n" gives [""].
310         tokens.truncate(top.min(tokens.len().max(1)));
311         // Actually truncate to top, but if top > len, use all.
312         if top < tokens.len() {
313             tokens.truncate(top);
314         }
315         tokens
316     }
317 }

320     use rand::seq::SliceRandom;
321     use rand::thread_rng;
322     let mut rng = thread_rng();
323     let mut picked: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
324     for _ in 0..combi {
325         if let Some(choice) = pool.choose(&mut rng) {
326             picked.push(choice.clone());
327         }
328     }
329     let mut repeated: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
330     for _ in 0..rep {
331         for p in &picked {
332             repeated.push(p.clone());
333         }
334     }
335     let mut s = repeated.join(" ");
336     s.push(' ');
337     s

fn load_pool(n_str: &str, top: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    if n_str == "2" {
        let mut v: Vec<String> = crate::ngrams::BIGRAMS.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
        v.truncate(top.min(v.len()));
        v
    } else if n_str == "3" {
        let mut v: Vec<String> = crate::ngrams::TRIGRAMS.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
        v.truncate(top.min(v.len()));
        v
    } else if n_str == "4" {
        let mut v: Vec<String> = crate::ngrams::TETRAGRAMS.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
        v.truncate(top.min(v.len()));
        v
    } else if n_str == "w" {
        let mut v: Vec<String> = crate::ngrams::WORDS.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
        v.truncate(top.min(v.len()));
        v
    } else {
        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(n_str).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut tokens: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        for line in content.lines() {
            for part in line.split(',') {
                let filtered: String = part.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control()).collect();
                tokens.push(filtered);
            }
        }
        tokens.truncate(top.min(tokens.len().max(1).max(tokens.len())));
        // Actually truncate to top (if top < len, truncate, else keep all). Since truncate handles top>len (no-op), just truncate(top).
        // The above line is messy, simplify:
        // tokens.truncate(top);
        // But we already did? Let's just do correctly:
        // (We already truncated above with min, but for empty, tokens empty, truncate does nothing)
        tokens
    }
}

fn generate_lesson(pool: &[String], combi: usize, rep: usize) -> String {
    use rand::seq::SliceRandom;
    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
    let mut picked: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..combi {
        if let Some(choice) = pool.choose(&mut rng) {
            picked.push(choice.clone());
        }
    }
    let mut repeated: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..rep {
        for q in &picked {
            repeated.push(q.clone());
        }
    }
    let mut s = repeated.join(" ");
    s.push(' ');
    s
}
